title: Claims Audit Memorandum: Earlier Unrepaired Roof Damage on a HomeGuard Homeowners Policy
content:
**Subject: roof surfacing money already paid on an earlier claim of the same HomeGuard Homeowners Policy and never repaired.**

Roof surfacing damage already paid on an earlier claim and never repaired is not paid twice. When wind or hail roof surfacing damage on a HomeGuard claim is re-settled from a below-deductible denial, the reversal payment is reduced by a deduction for earlier unrepaired roof damage, determined as follows.

## The rule

Look at the claims on the policy other than the claim being re-settled whose date of loss falls in the 36 months before the call, and at the roof surfacing entries on those earlier claims.

1. **Forfeited depreciation.** Where roof surfacing money was issued on the policy on such an earlier claim and the depreciation withheld on it has been forfeited, the deduction is the roof surfacing money issued on it.
2. **Standing holdback.** Where such money was issued and depreciation withheld on it still stands, neither released nor forfeited, the deduction is that money plus the standing holdback, which the earlier claim may still pay.
3. **Otherwise** nothing is deducted.

The rules are read in that order: where an earlier roof surfacing holdback in the window has been forfeited, rule 1 fixes the deduction. The deduction is taken from the reversal payment before the payment is floored at 0.00 and rounded to the cent.

## Terms used

- **Roof surfacing money issued**: the total of the roof surfacing payment entries on the earlier claims in the window.
- **Forfeited**: a forfeiture entry for withheld roof surfacing depreciation stands on the earlier claim.
- **Standing holdback**: roof surfacing depreciation withheld on the earlier claim, less what has been released and less what has been forfeited, is still above 0.00.
- **The window**: the date of loss of the earlier claim falls in the 36 months before the call. A claim whose date of loss is earlier than that is outside the window, whatever it paid.

## Decision grid

| Earlier roof surfacing money in the window | Withheld depreciation on it | Deduction |
|---|---|---|
| Issued | Forfeited | The roof surfacing money issued |
| Issued | Standing, neither released nor forfeited | The roof surfacing money issued plus the standing holdback |
| Issued | Fully released after repair | Nothing |
| None issued | Any | Nothing |

## Illustrations (hypothetical figures)

- An earlier hail claim, loss dated 20 months before the call, paid 4200.00 on its roof surfacing and withheld 1800.00, which was forfeited when no proof of repair arrived. Deduction: 4200.00.
- The same earlier claim, but its 1800.00 holdback is still standing. Deduction: 4200.00 plus 1800.00, which is 6000.00.
- The same earlier claim, but the whole 1800.00 was released against proof of a new roof. The earlier damage was repaired: nothing is deducted.
- An earlier roof surfacing payment on a claim with a loss dated 37 months before the call lies outside the 36 months: nothing is deducted for it.
